title: Runtime precision switching for KV cache with calibration feedback loop
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement and evaluate a runtime controller that switches KV cache precision between INT8 and FP8 (and back) based on recent decoding stability and a lightweight calibration feedback signal. This ticket covers experiment harness, controller prototype in the serving runtime, offline calibration feedback loop that tunes hysteresis thresholds, and accuracy/latency validation across representative workloads.

Motivation: Static quantization profiles (always INT8 or always FP8) either leave latency on the table or risk unnecessary quality regressions for bursty/variable prompts. A small hysteresis controller that opportunistically uses INT8 for stable prefixes but falls back to FP8 when drift is detected could gain ~10-30% token latency savings while keeping end-user quality within SLOs.

Scope:
- Build experiment harness that can replay production-like traces and measure per-token latency and quality deltas for INT8, FP8, and hybrid runtime switching.
- Implement prototype precision-switching controller in staging runtime (config flag gated).
- Integrate a calibration feedback loop that updates controller thresholds from daily calibration runs.
- Evaluate on 3 model families (7B, 13B, 70B) with 3 prompt cohorts (chatty long prefix, instructions, short queries).
- Produce dashboards and a PR with runtime changes and configuration docs.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible harness that compares INT8/FP8/hybrid on stored traces (scripts + sample traces checked in)
Prototype controller implemented behind a runtime feature flag and validated in staging for 48h
Calibration pipeline produces threshold recommendations and these are applied by the controller with audit logs
End-to-end results show <=0.8% avg QA exact-match regression (or explainable upstream distribution skew) while achieving >=12% token-latency reduction on median workloads
PR merged for runtime changes (with tests) and a follow-up rollout plan documented

decisions: Use a two-state hysteresis controller (INT8 <-> FP8) rather than per-layer mixed precision to reduce runtime complexity and certification surface.
Signal: use rolling KL-divergence over logits + token-level loss proxy (teacher logit alignment on calibration set) as primary drift detector.
Calibration loop: nightly offline runs on held-out prompt cohorts to recommend thresholds; engineer override allowed via console.
Safety: controller will never switch to INT8 on first N tokens (N configurable, default=8) to avoid cold-start regressions.
Rollout: staged canary -> 1% production with monitoring alarms set for quality regression (>1.5% EM drop) and latency SLO violations.
